assertions.source: Of the 2 of 3 observables that were actually EVALUATED, 0 close A≥3. description: Derive-or-refute: does B = ρ·[Vol(atom)−Vol(free)] close A≥3 binding, using DERIVED volumes (no census-knot fit)? Three observables all fail: (A) log|tr_M| volume — no derived ρ closes it (−55…−90%); (B) cosh-inversion — every |tr_M|<2 (elliptic), no real length; (C) SnapPy on the derived word's 2^(2A+1) sign-branch closures — EVALUATED 2026-09-07 (qou-m6gp): the per-nucleon pieces ARE hyperbolic (2-component links, Vol 4.75–16.19), but every inter-nucleon interface is a single letter, so each atom branch closure is the connected sum of its nucleon pieces and Vol(atom) − Vol(free) ≡ 0 by additivity of simplicial volume; B_C = ρ·0 = 0 for every ρ (−100 %). Scope-(b) on the DIFFERENCE only; an absolute-volume reading is NOT excluded. The earlier 'non-hyperbolic, Vol≈0' wording was never measured and is wrong for the live (alternating-core) word.
